Hi I am trying to teach my kid who is into Rubik's cube and who is familiar with the other Lean games (and loves them). So, I was introducing group theory to her and crafted the Rubik's cube group theory game locally. I wonder if there is an appetite for this for other people? Can someone also suggest me a world building path for this? I am going to roughly follow this https://people.math.harvard.edu/~jjchen/docs/Group%20Theory%20and%20the%20Rubik%27s%20Cube.pdf


If anyone wants to try super early beta and give feedback: https://adam.math.hhu.de/#/g/code-cntrl/rubiks-cube-game

Specifically for "is anyone else interested in Lean for Rubik's cube group theory": yes! :raising_hand:
(not sure about the other questions)
Did you play around with the game? Any feedback? I’m working on more worlds!
I'm not a fan of the idea of teaching group theory using the cube, sorry

Would Lean the programming language be up to finding optimal solves for random scrambles? You could create a database of all positions obtainable from the solved position after 10 moves and then start moving from the scramble until one falls into the database. Could writing this code be turned into a game somehow?
